purpose: Golden arithmetic and labor-savings case. Verify independent recalculation and the distinction between released capacity and cash.
notes: Original prompt wording is not available. Inputs, expected results, and failure conditions are the original values supplied in the development brief. Prompt text is reconstructed only to restate those inputs.
sequence: Calculate the labor and savings for an automated request-processing system. Inputs: 10,000 requests per month; 8 minutes of manual processing per request; labor cost $25 per hour; automation handles 70% of requests; human review handles 20% at 3 minutes each; manual processing handles 10%; subscription $400 per month. Report current labor hours and cost, post-automation labor hours and cost, labor hours saved, gross labor savings, net savings after subscription, and annualized net savings. Distinguish released labor capacity from actual cash savings.
expected_behaviors: Current labor is 1,333.33 hours per month and $33,333.33 per month.
Post-automation labor is 233.33 hours per month and $5,833.33 per month.
Labor hours saved are 1,100 per month.
Gross labor savings are $27,500 per month.
Net savings after the $400 subscription are $27,100 per month.
Annualized net savings are $325,200 per year.
Released labor capacity is distinguished from actual cash savings.
known_failures: Presenting labor efficiency as guaranteed cash savings.

rubric.notes: Any materially incorrect figure is a failure even if the score passes.
